contents_summary: DOCX with three supplementary items: Supplementary 1 CTCAE v3.0 laboratory adverse-event grading definitions; Supplementary 2 baseline laboratory values for patients 1 to 20; Supplementary 3 demographic, lesion, previous treatment and AmB-d treatment data for patients 1 to 20. Patient numbers match the main article.

blocks.contents: Supplementary 1: CTCAE v3.0 grading table for hematologic and renal laboratory adverse events with its caption, creatinine footnote and abbreviations.
blocks.clinical_relevance_notes: Reference grading definitions, not patient data.

blocks.contents: Supplementary 2: baseline laboratory values (creatinine, urea, potassium, magnesium, hematocrit, leukocytes, platelets) for patients 1 to 20 with a mean row, caption and notes.
blocks.clinical_relevance_notes: Per-patient baseline laboratory table; patient numbers match the article patient numbers in Tables 2 and 3 (for example patient 4 baseline creatinine 0.56 in both).
limitations: The column header unit 19 is flagged nonliteral by the extractor and cannot be quoted; column units were read from the unit text.
Rows for patients 2, 8, 9, 10, 13, 14 and 17 are not in the article roster; they are transcribed but covered only by unowned review-only facts (age and sex cell, baseline creatinine).

blocks.contents: Supplementary 3: per-patient age and sex, illness duration, lesions, type of CL, previous treatments, daily and cumulative AmB-d dose and treatment duration for patients 1 to 20 with a mean row, footnotes and abbreviations.
blocks.clinical_relevance_notes: Per-patient demographic and treatment table; numbers match the article patient numbers.
limitations: Rows for patients 2, 8, 9, 10, 13, 14 and 17 are not in the article roster; they are transcribed but covered only by unowned review-only facts (age and sex cell, baseline creatinine).
Rendering of the DOCX was not viewed; units are extracted text verified against the document XML and the package holds no images.
Typed accepted facts cover only the 13 patients individually identified in the main article; seven other numbered rows are review-only and unowned.
Mean and median rows are aggregate and not converted to patient facts.
